open_points.subject: OwnerFormField destination
open_points.text: whether it belongs to the request or to its values
open_points.question: How does a row identify the exact destination it fills, including nested paths and tuple positions?
options: Only top-level request and value fields exist, so the field name is the complete destination
Restore an explicit destination path and tuple-position markers in each row
Define a separate mapping from field names to destinations
open_points.default_guess: Treat the field name as a top-level key in either the request or its values.

witness.initial: An owner request contains two nested or positional values that cannot both be identified by a top-level field name alone.
events: The owner submits a form field.
The owner interface looks up the row and tries to place the parsed value into the request.
outcomes: The interface treats the name as a top-level key.
The interface uses an unstated nested path or tuple position.
witness.observer: The owner or downstream request handler sees a different request.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField name uniqueness
open_points.question: Must field names be unique across the whole owner form table, or may rows with different destinations or reading kinds share a name?
options: Require every row name to be globally unique
Allow the same name once under the request and once under values
Allow duplicate names and define a disambiguation rule
open_points.default_guess: Require every row name to be globally unique.

witness.initial: The table contains two rows named limit, one belonging to the request and one to its values.
events: The reader selects a row by the submitted name.
outcomes: The release is refused because names must be unique.
The reader accepts both rows and chooses one using an unstated rule.
witness.observer: The owner sees either a rejected release or a differently populated request.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField name uniqueness invariant
open_points.question: If field-name uniqueness is required, what must its Required tests item show?
options: Show that a table containing two rows with the same name is rejected
Show uniqueness only within each of request and values
Do not impose name uniqueness
open_points.default_guess: Show that any two rows with the same name make the release invalid.

open_points.subject: closed-list field reading
open_points.text: as one of a closed list
open_points.question: Where does each such row identify the particular closed list and its allowed members?
options: Add the enumeration identity to the row
Use one global closed list for all such fields
Define an external field-name-to-enumeration mapping
open_points.default_guess: Add the enumeration identity to each closed-list row.

witness.initial: Two owner fields use different closed lists, and both rows state only that their text is read as one of a closed list.
events: The owner submits a value valid for the first list but not the second.
The reader parses the second field.
outcomes: The reader accepts the value using the first list.
The reader refuses it using the second list.
witness.observer: The owner sees acceptance or refusal of the same submission.

open_points.subject: whole-number parsing
open_points.question: Which textual forms count as a whole number, and what required result occurs when the text does not count?
options: Accept only canonical unsigned decimal text and refuse anything else
Accept signed decimal integers and refuse anything else
Use the implementation language's integer parser and propagate or translate its failure
open_points.default_guess: Accept canonical unsigned decimal text and refuse invalid input without processing the request.

witness.initial: A whole-number field contains the text -1 or 01.
events: The owner interface reads the field.
outcomes: The interface accepts and produces an integer.
The interface refuses the submission as noncanonical or outside the allowed domain.
witness.observer: The owner sees acceptance or refusal.

open_points.subject: yes-or-no parsing
open_points.question: Which submitted strings represent yes and no, and what required result occurs for every other string?
options: Accept only the literal page values yes and no
Accept true and false
Accept a case-insensitive or broader set of boolean spellings
open_points.default_guess: Accept only the exact values yes and no and refuse all others.

events: The owner interface reads the field.
outcomes: The interface treats true as yes.
The interface refuses true because only yes and no are valid.
witness.observer: The owner sees acceptance or refusal.

open_points.subject: closed-list parsing failure
open_points.text: as one of a closed list
open_points.question: What must the owner interface do when submitted text is not a member of the field's closed list?
options: Refuse the entire request without effects
Ignore the field
Substitute a default member
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the entire request without effects.

witness.initial: A closed-list field is submitted with a value outside its list.
events: The owner interface reads the field.
outcomes: The request is refused without effects.
The invalid field is ignored or replaced and the request proceeds.
witness.observer: The owner and any observer of downstream effects see the difference.

open_points.subject: unlisted submitted fields
open_points.question: What happens when the owner submits a field for which the table has no row?
options: Ignore the unlisted field
Refuse the request
Pass the field through as unparsed text

witness.initial: The submitted form contains an extra field named admin that has no table row.
events: The owner interface processes the submitted fields.
outcomes: The interface refuses the request or passes admin downstream.
witness.observer: The owner or downstream handler sees the difference.

open_points.subject: duplicate submitted values
open_points.question: If the submission contains the same field name more than once, which value is read or is the submission refused?
options: Refuse duplicate submitted names
Use the first value
Use the last value
Read all values

witness.initial: The form submission contains limit=1 followed by limit=100.
outcomes: The interface produces 100 or refuses the duplicate.
witness.observer: The owner or downstream request handler sees a different result.

open_points.subject: absent form fields
open_points.question: Does every table row describe a required submitted field, and what happens when a named field is absent?
options: Every row is required and absence refuses the request
Every row is optional and absence leaves its destination unset
Requiredness is an additional fact of each row
open_points.default_guess: Treat rows as optional because the model contains no requiredness fact.

witness.initial: The table has a row named limit, but the owner omits limit from the form.
events: The owner interface processes the missing field.
outcomes: The interface accepts the request with limit unset.
The interface refuses the request because limit is required.
witness.observer: The owner sees acceptance or refusal.

open_points.subject: owner form table provider symbol
open_points.text: The release: the owner form table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: Which emitted data-provider symbol supplies this table to generated code?
options: Keep the previously named OWNER_FORM_FIELDS constant
Emit and import a differently named provider constant
consequences: Keeping OWNER_FORM_FIELDS preserves a stable import name for later notes and generated modules
Choosing another symbol requires generation and every consuming note or import to agree on that symbol
open_points.requirement: The release: the owner form table the data provider holds.
